subject: HorizonCloud — deployment readout and next technical asks
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Samira Patel <samira@horizoncloud.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro + live demo — quick summary and next steps

Hi Samira — thanks again for taking the call earlier. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can size a deployment and prepare procurement paperwork: 

Key pain points you shared:
- High inference cost and unpredictable latency during peak analytics jobs (batch of user prompts + reranking).
- Need to serve both real-time chat (low latency) and nightly bulk scoring (high throughput).
- Strict data residency and audit requirements for EU customers currently in scope.

Top goals for the pilot:
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 120 ms for interactive chat paths; p50 ~< 50 ms preferred.
- Throughput target: sustain 100 concurrent req/s for chat and 1k req/s for bulk scoring (batched).
- Support for an LLM that matches the internal safety filters and is compatible with quantized execution (target model: ~35–70B family, fine-tuning later).
- Private deployment behind your VPC with KMS integration for keys.

Immediate asks from HZ team to proceed:
1) Can you confirm the decision-makers for procurement and any lead times for PO/contract? (You mentioned procurement@horizoncloud.com — I’ll loop them in.)
2) Can you share a representative sample of request/response sizes (avg tokens in / out) and sequence length distribution for chat vs batch scoring? If you prefer, we can accept a sanitized CSV.
3) Any non-negotiable compliance controls we should be aware of (retention windows, IP restrictions, SOC2 evidence requirements)?

Next steps we propose:
- We’ll produce a short deployment readout with two options: (A) Dedicated cluster optimized for low-latency chat and batching; (B) Private VPC on your side with a smaller dedicated pool and burst to hosted capacity. Expect that readout within 48 hours.
- Schedule a 30-minute architecture sync next week with Marcus (infrastructure) and Monica (CS ops) to validate topology and handoff.

Attachments: none on this email.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the readout and book the sync.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Patel <samira@horizoncloud.com>, procurement@horizoncloud.com
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: HorizonCloud — deployment readout and next steps — architecture sketch + capacity estimates

Team / Samira — attaching the architecture sketch and the capacity spreadsheet. High-level technical readout below (concise):

Summary of recommended topology:
- Primary: Redwood Dedicated cluster (single-tenant) sized for low-latency interactive traffic. Baseline configuration: 8x H100 80GB (or equivalent A100 v2 if H100 not available), weights sharded across GPUs with tensor-parallel execution. Model baseline: 35–70B family quantized to 4-bit (QLoRA-compatible) to hit memory targets and maintain generation quality.
- Secondary: Nightly batch scoring on a dedicated worker pool (same infra but batched at 512–1024 tokens with large continuous batching windows). Burst policy: allow spiky batch jobs to use warm hosted capacity for short periods (policy-controlled).

Performance expectations (assumptions: 2048 max seq, avg chat seq 256, p95 seq 1024 until Samira’s data):
- Interactive path (no heavy context rerankers): p50 token latency ~6–8 ms; p95 token latency ~20–25 ms. For a typical response of 60 tokens, estimated p50 response latency ~40–60 ms, p95 response latency ~100–130 ms depending on concurrency and KV cache hit rate.
- Throughput: cluster above can support ~120–150 interactive req/s with continuous batching and smart routing. Bulk scoring (batched) throughput depends on batch size; expect several thousand requests per minute when batched efficiently.

Operational notes / features to include:
- Prefix KV cache for common user context to reduce decode tokens and latency.
- Autoscaling policy: target 70% util for steady-state; aggressive burst queue up to 120% with pre-warmed instances.
- Canary rollout plan: start with 5% traffic to new model variant, monitor quality via shadow evals and automatic rollback on quality regression.
- Compliance: we can deploy in your VPC with KMS HSM integration and provide admin audit logs (retention configurable, default 2 years).

Risks & mitigations:
- Cold KV cache: mitigate with small warmup traffic and synthetic priming set during rollout.
- Long-sequence spikes: apply per-request sequence-length caps and early-truncation policies for interactive paths; route large sequences to batch workers.

Deliverables attached:
- architecture-sketch.pdf (sketch with cluster layout, network flows, and KMS integration)
- capacity-estimates.xlsx (cost model for Dedicated vs Private VPC options)

Next recommended steps:
1) Review attachments and confirm whether HorizonCloud prefers Dedicated (simpler SLA) or Private VPC (compliance control).
2) We’ll produce a short SOW draft and preliminary pricing once you pick a preferred deployment model.
3) Schedule procurement + legal call if needed.

Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
